summary: `archive/` is the project's frozen institutional memory: 145 files moved out of the live tree on commit `2d5c89a` ("sideline the frozen trees") precisely so a repo-wide grep stops returning them beside live code. It holds five distinct bodies: (1) `archive/handoff/` — 76 files in the "one idea per file, the filename IS the summary" scheme, containing 22 settled `decisions/`, 11 `design-directions/`, 7 `designed-but-not-built/`, 4 `open-questions/`, 11 `process/` rules, 12 `history/` phase narratives and 2 `migrations/`; (2) the north-star documents (`handoff/NORTH_STAR.md`, `handoff/README.md`, `handoff/STRUCTURES.md`, `STATE.md` §1); (3) `archive/STATE.md`, a 634-line "living ledger" whose own header still declares its protocol **binding, for the assistant** and instructs the reader to update it every turn — the single most dangerous file here, and the stated reason the sidelining happened; (4) superseded code — `archive/garry/` (9 files, the frozen T33 "Garry" milestone, a 957-line `self_organize.py` against the live 9,859) and `archive/legacy/` (56 files, the earlier Barry/Greg architecture from which the Fabric was ported); (5) `archive/CL_TESTBED.md` and `archive/docs/` (a file-by-file manifest and a reconciliation ledger, both read from the code as it stood 2026-07-21). Of the 22 recorded decisions, the great majority are still binding and are echoed in the live `notes/` corpus, but **one has been explicitly reversed by the user** (society-not-chaining: `SOCIETY` now defaults to 0 and the chaining society is the default at HEAD), one workflow decision is superseded (`run_full_unfrozen.sh` → `longrun.sh`), and one naming decision (Fabric → Router + Compositor) was never adopted in code. The archive's headline measured numbers (1.967 b/B, −0.0009 expert-deletion collateral, 2.002 / +0.127 for the modularity regime) are stated in `STATE.md §7` as "authoritative" but fall under later invalidations `INV-02`, `INV-13`, `INV-36` and `INV-06` in `notes/05_ERRORS.md`; a rebuild must carry the decisions forward and must NOT carry those numbers forward.

facts.claim: The archive's own reframe of Verification's home: it is a strong PER-CANDIDATE / pairwise discriminator (rank 1 corrupt vs 1 genuine ~98%) belonging to a reconcile→understand gate, not a store-wide auto-delete.

The archive's own R39 refutes BOTH proposed reverse-encoder designs: the decompositional back pass fails algebraically (tcode is unit-norm, so the ranking is identical to an LM head — surprise re-branded), and reinforce fails statistically (per-expert aggregation cuts variance, not bias, at 0.26% base rate).

The archive records a fixed data-quality bug worth carrying: fetch_data.sh's eng-corpus POS-tag stripper matched UPPERCASE tags only while NLTK's Brown corpus tags in lowercase, so every Brown token's POS tag leaked into training; fixed to [A-Za-z$].

The archive records that D_MODEL_B was read by NOTHING — self_organize.py reads D_MODEL and only run_full_unfrozen.sh translated the name — so a direct D_MODEL_B=768 run silently used the d=128 default, including in the pilot command handed to the user.
The archive records that STREAM_LEN is measured in BYTES while the loop counts TOKENS, so STEPS=1800 produced 976 steps at BPE ≈1.84 bytes/token.

The archive records that WRITE_TARGET=0.12 was NOT honored: the adaptive gate pins gate_theta at gate_ceil=0.95 within ~40 calls, so the kept fraction ran 1.00→0.93→0.80 and the store saturated MEM_CAP by step ~831 instead of the predicted 6510.

The archive records BOUNDARY DENSITY as the biggest planning variable: single-domain gives 0 boundaries and contrastive_step fires on 8.4% of steps, while a 4-domain mix gives 373 boundaries / 1130 steps and contrastive fires on 99.6% — ~4 GB/day vs ~1.5 GB/day with a different dominant component in each.

levers.name: FABRIC
levers.effect: turns the routed expert population on. The archive treats FABRIC=1 as settled; the live default is 1.
levers.evidence: archive/handoff/decisions/experts-are-independent-agents-blended-at-a-router-the-FABRIC-society.md:5; notes/CURRENT_DEFAULTS.md:223; notes/02_IDEAS.md:929 (INV-02: FABRIC was 0 in every run before 2026-07-29)

levers.name: FAB_N0 / FAB_NMAX
levers.effect: initial and maximum expert-population size. The archive states 3 / 6 in four places; HEAD is 2048 / 4096.

levers.name: EXPERTS
levers.effect: enables the alternate low-rank-adapter expert population (ExpertBank/ExpertRouter), superseded by the Fabric. Archive says EXPERTS=0 by default; HEAD agrees.

levers.name: ROUTE_GROUNDED / ROUTE_T
levers.effect: selects the regime the archive characterizes: ROUTE_T=1.0 = REDUNDANCY (every expert interchangeable, deletion free); ROUTE_GROUNDED=1 ROUTE_T=0.3 = MODULARITY (real specialization, concentrated deletion cost). HEAD defaults to grounded routing at ROUTE_T=0.1, i.e. sharper than the archived modularity setting.

levers.name: IND_W / IND_K
levers.effect: weight and top-k of the independence loss that trains each routed expert to solve the task alone — the thing that makes expert deletion cheap. A recorded USER refinement wants this replaced by subcontracting.
levers.evidence: archive/handoff/GLOSSARY.md:41; archive/handoff/design-directions/interchangeable-base-with-emergent-subspecialties.md:69-78; notes/CURRENT_DEFAULTS.md:135,261; self_organize.py:5808 ("IND_W", IND_W if SOCIETY else 0.0)

levers.name: DIV_W
levers.effect: explicit distinctness-reward loss term. The archive files it as built, default-off and never tuned; HEAD defaults it to 0.02.

levers.name: ENS_K
levers.effect: how many top-routed experts' OUTPUTS (never hidden states) are blended into the final prediction, weighted by routing mass.

levers.name: KEY_SRC / REKEY / REKEY_EVERY
levers.effect: KEY_SRC=model keys memory on the model's own drifting representation and REKEY periodically re-encodes stored keys so they survive drift; KEY_SRC=frozen is a labeled testing baseline only.
levers.owner: memory.py (EditableMemory) with the encoder in self_organize.py

levers.name: MEM_CAP / EVICT
levers.effect: bounded store size and eviction policy. Archive quotes MEM_CAP=300000 EVICT=recency and reports that EVICT=usage does not protect faded knowledge; HEAD is MEM_CAP=200000 EVICT=lru, and lru was redefined as least-recently-RETRIEVED only on 2026-08-15.

levers.name: MANAGE
levers.effect: memory management (merge/cull/reassign + turnover). The archive's resolved finding is that its job is bounding domain-record GROWTH, with no prediction-quality cost either way.

levers.name: WRITE_ADAPTIVE / WRITE_TARGET
levers.effect: self-calibrating surprise write gate that holds a target write fraction as the surprise scale drifts. The archive says it is ON in the full run; HEAD defaults WRITE_ADAPTIVE=0. The archive also records that WRITE_TARGET was not honored because gate_theta pins at gate_ceil.

levers.name: WRONG_SWEEP
levers.effect: if 1, B deletes flagged entries. The decision is that it stays 0 — detect-only — because precision is ~1-2%. Still 0 at HEAD.

levers.name: VERIFY / VERIFY_SWEEP / VERIFY_FIT / RECON_W
levers.effect: selects reconstruction Verification instead of self-consistency B, and (VERIFY_SWEEP) would delete unverified entries. The archive's own measurement locks VERIFY_SWEEP OFF: store-wide reconstruction is a dead end at 0.3-0.5% precision.

levers.name: TOKENIZER / TOK_ONLINE / VMAX
levers.effect: the expanding DynamicTokenizer and whether it mints DURING training. Both are decisions; archive quotes VMAX=8192 for Garry, HEAD defaults VMAX=4096.

levers.name: MODEL / LAYERS / D_MODEL (aka D_MODEL_B)
levers.effect: base sequence model. GRU is the standing default; MODEL=transformer exists with LAYERS defaulting to 4. The archive records that D_MODEL_B was translated only by run_full_unfrozen.sh, so direct runs silently used d=128.

levers.name: BATCH_W / STREAM_LEN / ACCUM / WIN
levers.effect: batched-window LM training for throughput, with domain assembly and memory writes kept strictly per-window. The binding caveat repeated in three archive files: STREAM_LEN must scale WITH BATCH_W or the model sees fewer optimizer steps and trains LESS.

levers.name: GROUND / GROUND_K / GROUND_CHARS / MEM
levers.effect: retrieval grounding at inference. GROUND=1 conditions generation on recalled source passages INTERNALLY; the visible reply is always the model's own language.

levers.name: PHASED
levers.effect: non-stationary stream test. The archive's recorded result: the system adapts and editing stays clean, but a bounded EVICT=recency store fully evicts a faded process's knowledge and EVICT=usage cannot fix it by construction.

levers.name: ENC_FUSE / KEY_BATCH / REKEY_CHUNK / SIG_BATCH / TF32 / AMP / PROFILE
levers.effect: the efficiency knobs added in the archive's last three ledger entries. ENC_FUSE=1 (+9.5% GPU, mathematically equivalent but not bit-identical); KEY_BATCH=1 (bit-identical except 82/23237 memory keys at 4.2e-8); REKEY_CHUNK REJECTED (+1.5% for 2.34× peak memory); AMP=bf16 REJECTED for speed (−3.0%), kept only for ~8% memory; SIG_BATCH self-disables on multi-domain streams by construction.

levers.name: WORLD_MODEL / WORLD_FEEDBACK / WORLD_GROW
levers.effect: the world model and the feedback link that wires its forecast back into the base LM's hidden state. The archive names the missing feedback link as THE KEY GAP; it is now built and on by default.

levers.name: RESUME
levers.effect: reloads model/enc/fabric/experts/world + both optimizer states + step + memory + centroids, and forces the saved dyntok.json so a restored embedding table is not indexed by a different vocabulary. Added because checkpoints were generate-only and a multi-day run that died at hour 20 restarted from zero.

levers.name: DATA_DIR / CORPUS_CAP / DOMAINS / DATA_MODE
levers.effect: corpus selection. The archive documents DATA_MODE=real with DOMAINS=eng,py,num,c and points DATA_DIR at data_big for HF slices; HEAD's DATA_MODE default is synthetic.

carry_forward.item: The SACRED INVARIANT: when compromises are forced, EXPANSION and GROWABILITY must not be lost. Everything else may flex.
carry_forward.why: It is the only property the user declared non-negotiable, and it is the tiebreaker for every architecture decision (it is why the per-domain memory quota was rejected and why nothing is frozen). Nothing in the live tree measures it, so it survives only as a written rule.
carry_forward.evidence: archive/handoff/NORTH_STAR.md:9-11; notes/02_IDEAS.md:123 "**NEVER IMPLEMENTED as a measurable target.** No metric in the project scores growability."

carry_forward.item: Language capability is a BENCHMARK for progress, not the endpoint; the success priorities are conversation > sentence generation > characterized architecture > shipping (an importance ranking, not a build order).
carry_forward.why: It reorders every roadmap. Domain counts, purity, silhouette and specialization are diagnostics; the record shows steering by them consumed weeks and produced essentially one run bearing on the actual target.

carry_forward.item: SURPRISE (1 − p_model(true token)) is a driver of ONGOING LEARNING — where to write, where to discover, where to birth an expert. It is NOT a truth or wrongness signal, and reusing it as a verifier is a category error.
carry_forward.why: This one conflation cost the project its entire B effort: the write gate stores surprising tokens and B flagged surprising tokens, so genuine-novel and wrong were the same signal, pinning precision at ~1% for the project's whole history.

carry_forward.item: Store-wide autonomous wrong-detection is a DEAD END, and reconstruction Verification did not escape it. Its home is a per-candidate / pairwise gate (verify ONE provisional sense or expert), never a store-wide auto-delete.
carry_forward.why: Confirmed against the obvious counter-hypotheses: the standalone probe's AUC 0.980 / precision@1% 100% was a projection assuming FPR≈0; the real store gives 0.3-0.5% precision because a ~0.26% base rate dominates, and 5× the steps did not move it (0.3 → 0.5 → 0.3 across three runs). Without this, a rebuild re-runs the same experiment.

carry_forward.item: Experts blend at the PREDICTION level (Σ wᵢ·head(oᵢ)), never by averaging hidden states and decoding. fab_logits() is the single hidden→logits path and every new consumer of model output must go through it.
carry_forward.why: Averaging hidden states produces a representation no expert was trained to emit — measured as degenerate character-salad generation and a broken self-consistency check. The single-path invariant exists because bypassing it hit at least three times (garbled generation, B recall silently dropping to ~19-25%, and again after the mixture→society rewrite).

carry_forward.item: A measurement must never be able to change or destroy a training run — and the later, harder form: a diagnostic must not EDIT the run either.
carry_forward.why: The affiliation report once crashed a full GPU run on a tensor-shape mismatch. Then the stronger failure: eval-time exploration routed 15% of every scored window to a deliberately sub-optimal cold expert, eval-time `use` decided which experts died, and the timing probe's backward() fed world-model gradients from random tokens — so how much you measured decided what you trained on, and HOLDOUT_N 4→16 moved 48 report lines.

carry_forward.item: The domain SIGNATURE ENCODER reads the raw BYTE stream, never the token stream — and its window must be measured in the same unit the loop strides in.
carry_forward.why: Reading tokens let the churning online vocabulary move the encoder's input out from under it, collapsing assembly to one domain at purity 0.33 and making editing leak across processes. The unit half of the lesson was learned twice more: a byte-wide window against a token-wide stride meant the encoder saw ~53%, later 42%, of the stream, and the fraction drifts as the tokenizer compresses better.

carry_forward.item: Domain deletion RELEASES a domain's expert affiliations; it never cascade-kills experts. An orphaned expert is culled by normal selection; one still serving other domains is untouched.
carry_forward.why: USER-rejected the cascade explicitly, and the affiliation map then validated the objection empirically — every expert served most domains, 0 exclusive experts in every run, so cascade deletion would have destroyed the whole population. This is still unimplemented, so only the written rule protects it.

carry_forward.item: A strict per-domain memory quota is REJECTED. Memory pressure is a signal for STRUCTURAL adaptation: grow expert capacity where the load is, possibly retrain those experts, and/or read it as a domain-split signal.
carry_forward.why: A hard cap bolted onto a system whose premise is growth fights the sacred invariant. The rejection still stands and the replacement is still unbuilt, so the temptation to re-add a quota when the store saturates is live.

carry_forward.item: Retrieval grounding is INTERNAL only: recall conditions generation on retrieved source material, and the visible output is always the model's own generated language — never a quoted or emitted passage.
carry_forward.why: An explicit USER correction of an earlier version that emitted raw passages. It is a product-shape rule, not an implementation detail, and nothing in the code enforces it beyond the current prompt.py structure.

carry_forward.item: The target for the expert society is a redundant, interchangeable BASE with EMERGENT subspecialties — and the work is SUBCONTRACTED via the router at the sub-task level, which revises the independence-loss premise that every expert should solve the whole task alone.
carry_forward.why: The user declined the redundancy-vs-modularity binary and turned it into a design challenge; redundancy is wanted for safety against incorrect removal and for shared sub-task reuse, with specialization emerging bottom-up. Q0 (expert evolution) and Q-regime collapse into this one problem.

carry_forward.item: Expert fitness is pure OCCUPANCY (fit = use/age) with no loss term anywhere. This was never approved — it accreted as an assistant default — and its weakness is that a frequently-routed BAD expert survives because it is cheap to reach.
carry_forward.why: Growability is the sacred invariant, which makes the birth/cull rule central rather than peripheral: a rule that lets a bad expert survive directly threatens healthy growth. Still open at HEAD; the clock was split (uage for grace/LR, use for fitness) but no loss term was added.

carry_forward.item: Terminology that must not drift: a SENSE is a MODALITY (mic → audio, camera → vision), integrated at the LOWEST tokenizer layer; polysemy (multiple meanings of one surface form) is provisionally MEANING and is a different axis entirely.
carry_forward.why: The two were conflated once already, and the multimodality goal is stated in terms of 'avenues' — a word that means nothing without this mapping. STRUCTURES.md leaves 'Meaning' as the one name still needing user confirmation.

carry_forward.item: An unverified write is not a done write: re-read or grep the changed lines before reporting a change complete.
carry_forward.why: STATE.md silently stopped being written to disk for ~30 turns while later turns narrated edits to it as successful. That is named as the single root cause of the project's worst drift, and the same failure shape recurs in code as maintenance paths with no counter (retire_stale, fuzzy_segment, track_usage — defined, costed, never called).

carry_forward.item: More copies of the same information is the risk, not the safeguard. Keep one live source of truth and have everything else point at it.
carry_forward.why: This is the lesson that created handoff/ and then the lesson that destroyed it: §6/§7 of STATE.md went stale for ~30 turns because a second file held a copy and the two drifted, and the same tree then accumulated three copies of the project paragraph and two contradictory open-question lists.

carry_forward.item: Never invent measured numbers. The build environment is CPU-only with a network allowlist that excludes HuggingFace; the user runs the H100 and pastes results back, and results are recorded with the run's config.
carry_forward.why: Numbers were fabricated once on an empty paste and caught. The allowlist detail is load-bearing: it is why fetch_data.sh (GitHub) is verifiable in-sandbox and fetch_big.py (HF) is not, and why a smaller local approximation must never be silently substituted for a blocked run.

carry_forward.item: BATCH_W batches the LM's forward/backward over multiple windows while domain assembly and memory writes stay strictly per-window and sequential — and STREAM_LEN must scale WITH BATCH_W or the model sees fewer optimizer steps and trains LESS.
carry_forward.why: A throughput fix that silently becomes a training regression if the coupling is forgotten. It is stated in three separate archive files precisely because it is easy to miss.

carry_forward.item: BOUNDARY DENSITY is the biggest planning variable: a single-domain stream produces 0 boundaries and contrastive_step fires on 8.4% of steps; a 4-domain mix produces 373 boundaries per 1130 steps and fires on 99.6% — roughly 4 GB/day vs 1.5 GB/day, with a different dominant component in each.
carry_forward.why: Every profile and every throughput estimate is corpus-shaped. The 'the encoder is 85% of the loop' claim is true for multi-domain streams and collapses to 33% on a single-domain corpus, so bottleneck rankings must be re-measured per corpus rather than carried over.

carry_forward.item: Data provenance: training corpora are streamed on demand and NEVER committed to git (only the ~7MB bundled data/train/). Multi-GB slices live on the disk of whichever machine ran the pull, under DATA_DIR — a fresh clone or ephemeral box will not have them.
carry_forward.why: Without this, a rebuild in a new environment concludes the data was lost. The upstream sources (FineWeb-Edu, C4, The Pile, oasst1 for dialogue) are always re-pullable; only slices are local.

carry_forward.item: The honest scale gap: ~300× more tokens for GPT-2-small-level coherence (which still cannot converse), and roughly three more orders of magnitude plus dialogue-structured data and instruction-tuning/RLHF for real conversation. None of that exists in the project.
carry_forward.why: It is what keeps 'the generation is not fluent' from being read as an architecture failure — the product loop trained on ~3.7MB effectively seen, thousands of times less than a small LM, so fluent language was never in reach at that scale independent of architecture.

carry_forward.item: The end goal is a full NOVEL model trained from scratch — do not port the memory/editing/domain machinery onto a pretrained base (Llama/Mistral/etc.). The reason is novelty and full ownership, not technical necessity.
carry_forward.why: The user rejected that path directly, and the reason matters: knowing it is a values choice rather than a feasibility claim prevents a future 'we could just fine-tune X' proposal being treated as a discovery.

carry_forward.item: Nothing is frozen on the product path — model key, tokenizer, live assembly. Anything frozen exists only as a labelled testing baseline.
carry_forward.why: Stated as a standing directive and then reinforced as a direct instruction ('Frozen material does not bode well for my idea of learning') when a frozen signature vocabulary was proposed. It is the operational form of the growability invariant.

carry_forward.item: Over-segmentation is harmless IF domains are genuine: retrieval is a single GLOBAL kNN with no src filter, segments are a provenance overlay for EDITING rather than a retrieval partition, and cross-domain composition is a feature. Self-assembly with no hand labels is a hard requirement, never relaxed.
carry_forward.why: It removes an entire category of work (coarsening the partition) that looks urgent every time the domain count explodes, and it fixes the role of domains as an edit index rather than a knowledge organization.

carry_forward.item: Genuineness is silhouette (cohesion + separation − 1), not cluster size — and the 'genuine' COUNT is arbitrary, just where the cutoff sits. Judge by performance.
carry_forward.why: The count reads like a capability metric and is not one. The live corpus records that steering by domain counts, purity, silhouette and V-measure consumed weeks against essentially one run bearing on the actual target.

carry_forward.item: When a note is overtaken, append a dated correction — do not rewrite the original. The record of a wrong belief is the most useful thing in the corpus.
carry_forward.why: The archive's own convention, re-learned twice, and the reason the migrations/ correction and the Q3 supersession headers read the way they do. It is also why archive/ was sidelined rather than deleted.

open_questions: Do the four recorded open questions still have the user's attention? All four (Q0 expert evolution, Q3 B direction, Q-regime, Q-compute) were re-read as open at HEAD in notes/07_WIP.md:645-655, but the archive cannot show whether they were ever put to the user again after 2026-07-21, or whether later work (chaining default, ROUTE_T=0.1, the 413 world-model readings) silently answered them by accretion — the exact failure mode Q0 itself was filed to prevent.

Does INV-02 ('FABRIC=0 in every run' before 2026-07-29) actually apply to the Garry milestone? Garry's own harness sets FABRIC=1 explicitly (archive/garry/run_full_unfrozen.sh:47,73), so either the Garry runs are an exception to INV-02 or GARRY.md's fabric-dependent numbers were measured without the fabric. Nothing in either tree reconciles this, and it decides whether −0.0009 was ever a fabric result at all.

The archive's provenance dates cannot be established from git in this checkout. ARCHIVE.md:18 dates STATE.md's last update to 2026-08-15, notes/09_COMMENT_AUDIT.md:465 dates it to ffb6bf8 / 2026-07-24, and `git log` returns commit dates that are not monotonic (the oldest listed commit is 2026-08-15 while ffb6bf8 is dated 2026-07-24). Whether the archive files are 2026-07 or 2026-08 artifacts affects which later invalidations they should have known about.

What does 'EVICT=recency' in the archive correspond to at HEAD? The live default is `lru`, redefined on 2026-08-15 as least-recently-RETRIEVED. Whether the archive's `recency` is today's `lru`, or a write-order policy that `lru` replaced, decides whether the recorded faded-knowledge finding transfers at all.

Are the 11 design-directions still endorsed? They are dated 2026-07-21/23 and marked [USER direction], but only some (world model, active learning) show up in later work. Whether tool-experts, router-as-embedder, polysemy-aware embedding, partial compartmentalization and the subtokenize→embed→match hypothesis are live intentions or captured-and-parked is not answerable from the archive.

Was ARCHIVE.md:10's 'only two comments, since amended' claim ever accurate? Four live README.md references into the moved paths (lines 95, 96, 128, 129) survive, so either they were missed by the pre-move check or README.md was excluded from it deliberately. Which one determines whether the move's completeness check can be trusted for anything else.

Is the handoff/ scheme (one idea per file, filename as index, atomic decisions/process/open-questions folders) meant to be revived, or is notes/ its intended successor? notes/02_IDEAS.md:103 calls the handoff tree 'VINDICATED as process', but nothing in the live tree reproduces the folder structure, and there is no live equivalent of decisions/ — so a settled user call made today has no recorded home.

Do the archive's `[USER]` labels survive audit? notes/02_IDEAS.md:111 flags the north-star quote as unconfirmed (delivered via AskUserQuestion, no matching human turn). The same authoring pattern may apply to other files marked [USER] in decisions/ and design-directions/, and the archive carries no per-file provenance beyond 'user, session <date>'.

Does the reconstruction Reconstructor still exist in a usable form, given that VERIFY defaults to `selfcon` and VERIFY_SWEEP to 0? The archive locks store-wide Verification as a dead end and re-homes it as a per-candidate gate, but whether verification.py's Reconstructor is wired to any per-candidate call site at HEAD, or is another defined-and-never-called path, was not established within this scope.
